label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: The shop refused every Add to cart with an error that asks to close the tab or disable extensions, on several products: that is how bot protection treats an automated browser. Not counted as an accessibility result.

reclassified.why: The shop refused every Add to cart with an error that asks to close the tab or disable extensions, on several products: that is how bot protection treats an automated browser.

findings.problem: After choosing a size and pressing Add to Bag the button says Adding, then an error text appears: we are sorry, this item cannot be added to your bag at the moment. The bag link still says currently empty. It happened on every try, so I could not reach checkout.

Same failure on a different product, with two sizes and three tries: the error text just appears in the page text, with no alert role or focus move, so a screen reader user may not hear it at all and has to re-read the page to notice it.

In the product list the main link of each product has no name at all, only the word link. The product name is plain text next to it. I could only open a product by guessing which unnamed link by position.
The colour swatches are radios but cannot take keyboard focus, so a keyboard user cannot change the colour at all. The size list also stays shown as expanded after a size is chosen.

The cookie banner needed two steps to dismiss and the page still announced the banner after pressing Deny Cookies until I re-read it. A second popup asking for country ([name]) stayed on top of the page and I had to find the Take me to the U.S. site button to get rid of it. Product image buttons are also named with raw HTML text like trade; and undefined.
